Post Award Quick Guide

The purpose of this Post Award Quick Guide is to: Establish the guidelines of the award using the Notice of Award; Determine which costs, expenses, and activities are allowable under the grant; Set up the award in Banner and introduce spending instruments; Discuss troublesome expenses and transactions that may lead to audit findings; Survey other matters of compliance; Define reporting requirements; Determine items requiring prior approval from the funding agency; Consider the resources available on www.morgan.edu/ora; Introduce the PI to the responsible officers at MSU

Self-paced ORA eTraining module. Source: https://rise.articulate.com/share/bLJYTO9HcIsvOpsVS9KKkClk3VoLSs1N

## Message from ORA
Congratulations on Your Award!
The Office of Research Administration is ready to provide support and guidance through the post-award administration of your project. We are excited to witness the impact that this grant will undoubtedly have on advancing knowledge and making a meaningful difference in your field. Your hard work and passion have truly paid off, and we couldn't be more proud of your well-deserved success! In this Post-Award module we will review topics ranging from cost allowability to requirements for reporting to funding agencies.
Contact Us
If you have any questions regarding the material covered, or any general questions regarding the operation of your grant, please feel encouraged to send an email to ask.ora@morgan.edu .

## Recap: What's Already Happened
Have We Received the Notice of Award (NOA)?
When we show up to the present moment with all of our senses, we invite the world to fill us with joy. The pains of the past are behind us. The future has yet to unfold. But the now is full of beauty simply waiting for our attention.
NOA Copy for PI
Does the PI for this project have a copy of the Notice of Award? The PI needs the NOA to verify the various facets of their project ranging from reporting requirements to the approved budget. The NOA may vary from the proposal submission so it is vital to ensure you, the PI, are aware of those changes and how they may affect your project.
NOA Copy for ora
The Office of Research Administration (ORA) also needs to have a copy of your Notice of Award on hand. They can help provide guidance on the various administrative functions both before and after the award is granted. Additionally, there may be factors such as cost share, negotiated indirect cost rates, and others that need to be reviewed and approved by the ORA.
noa copy for RFA
Restricted Funds Accounting (RFA) is the team on our campus responsible for invoicing requirements for projects and for loading your project into Banner. Neither of these vital actions can be taken without a copy of the Notice of Award. You will work closely with your assigned RFA grant accountant to report expenses to the funding agency, foundation, etc.

## Spending Instruments
How to Spend Your Money
The PI may spend award funds through a variety of mechanisms at MSU. These are summarized in PI Handbook #3 on pages 21-22. The PI must: Work with RFA to establish an award account with a Banner index and fund. Ensure a Purchasing Card (P-Card) is linked to the index/fund if needed. Submit a WorkFlow request for access to your project budget in Banner.

Establishing the Award Account
Has a Post-Award Briefing with the ORA been completed? Once ORA has a copy of the NOA in hand they will contact the project PI to schedule this meeting. No spending can occur on a project without this so be sure to make yourself available. Once the Post-Award Briefing has been completed, has notice been sent to the Restricted Funds Accounting (RFA) team? Has RFA set up the account and assigned a grant accountant? RFA needs to be notified that a Post-Award Briefing has occurred so that they can initiate actions in Banner to establish your award account. At that time, RFA will also assign the grant accountant you will work with for the duration of your award.
P-Card Access
Does the PI have a MSU Purchasing Card (P-Card)? If yes : Submit a request for the new index to be attached to the current P-Card through the Purchasing Card Office . If no: Submit a request for a new P-Card through the Purchasing Card Office if necessary. The PI (or other assigned cardholder) will need to receive P-Card training. Whether or not a PI receives a P-Card for their project is at the discretion of the MSU Purchasing Card Office.
Banner WorkFlow Access
Has the PI's supervisor submitted a WorkFlow request for the PI to gain access to their budget in Banner? Once Banner access is granted, the award funds may begin to be spent according to the budget/budget justification.
Knowledge check: True or False: As soon as you receive a copy of your Notice of Award you may begin spending on your project.
  - True  [incorrect]
  - False  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  Explanation: There are multiple reasons why this answer is false. First, your Notice of Award typically arrived before the start date of your project. Here at MSU, pre-award spending is typically not allowed. Additionally, RFA and ORA need to provide you with a post award briefing, and establish the project budget in Banner, before you can spend on your project.
Knowledge check: True or False: The Purchasing Card Office will automatically add your new budget to your existing purchasing card once ORA has received your Notice of Award.
  - True  [incorrect]
  - False  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  Explanation: You need to submit documentation to the P-Card Office to add the new Banner index associated with your project to your P-Card.

Knowledge check: Which specific groups need to review your project if it includes both human subjects AND animal research?
  - OHR & RFA  [incorrect]
  - IRB & IACUC  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  - ORA & RFA  [incorrect]
  - HHS & USDA  [incorrect]
  If correct: Great job! The IRB will review your project protocol compliance for human subjects research and IACUC will review your compliance with respect to using animals in research.
  If incorrect: While these other offices and groups may be involved in your project at one time or another, they are not actively involved in reviewing your project compliance with respect to human and animal research.

## When to Involve Your Funding Agency
Actions That May Require Prior Approval
While the PI has substantial latitude in executing the project, if there are changes to the initial plan, there are several items that may need prior approval from the funding agency. These items vary by the funding agency, and the Notice of Award, and may also change over the years. PI Handbook #3: Grant-Related Processes pages 58 – 64 has further details about "Deviations from the Original Plan." For example, NIH: the NIH may allow the PI to move substantial amounts of funds between budget lines (for example, from travel to supplies); indeed, moving up to 25% of funds is generally allowable for NIH awards. In fact, for the NIH, even more may be allowable as long as there is no change in scope. If you are not sure if the change you seek is allowable under your award, please email ask.ora@morgan.edu and be sure to include details about the suggested change and a copy of the Notice of Award.
Some salient examples of change in scope are: "Change in the specific aims approved at the time of award; Substitution of one animal model for another; Change from the approved use of live vertebrate animals; Change from the approved involvement of human subjects that would result in an increased risk…" For further information on the NIH's definition of the change of scope, please click here .

## Go Change the World!
ORA is Here for You
The Office of Research Administration would again like to congratulate you on receiving this funding. Our office prides itself on delivering the most optimal customer experience possible and we are excited to work with you on your project! Your work directly contributes to our skyrocket towards R1 Carnegie status and we couldn't be more appreciative. Some of you may have more support than others, but we want to encourage all of you to use our staff as a resource to help reduce your administrative burden so you can focus on what you do best: performing research that will change the world! If you have any questions related to your project please feel encouraged to contact us at ask.ora@morgan.edu .
